rv.q: Both women are wonderful paradoxes, people for whom artifice is truly natural, and as mother and daughter they communicate in a perfect private language to which we are allowed privileged access.
When the servants are just as winning as the leads, that tells you this is one regal and enjoyable “Royal Family.”
There's a beauty of one now in "The Royal Family," the classic 1927 comedy that George S. Kaufman and Edna Ferber wrote about three generations of a chaotic and madly gifted New York acting dynasty.
The production does find a workable comic footing, and its lead performers rise to the occasion in sparkling turns.
Thanks to Maxwell and Rogers, for the moment their bygone spirit is burning brightly once again.

Scenery-munching is allowed, and the cast's incisors are sharp, for the most part. Director Doug Hughes keeps the plots spinning smoothly. Reigning over the three-ring circus is grande dame Fanny (a restrained Rosemary Harris), who's been out of commission for two years but is ready for a comeback.
In the end, the actors pull it off, proving that when fine players such as these, in the tradition of the Barrymores, take to the stage, they are a delight to behold.

cn.t: This 1927 Kaufman-Ferber comedy about a theatrical dynasty gets a rousing, sumptuous revival with standout performances from Jan Maxwell and Reg Rogers, though ensemble work could be tighter and laughs don't always reach gale-force.

sg.ra: SeatPlan notes rows A-D are ideal at this 634-seat house: close enough to catch facial expressions but not neck-craning. Row AA also called out for superior legroom. No overhang concerns (Mezzanine overhang starts at row G per SeatPlan).

Headout and SeatPlan both flag rows E-J as the best price-to-sightline ratio: meaningfully cheaper than the A-D premium band while staying close in a 634-seat room. Slight orchestra rake keeps sightlines clean. Mezzanine overhang (per SeatPlan) begins at row G but the intimate room means no sound-deadening issue in this band.

sg.ra: SeatPlan confirms the Mezzanine overhangs from row G back, so K-Q sit fully under.
